newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end off, China plays under profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end off, China plays under profit-taking.

text.p: Late profit-taking in Hong Kong's hot red-chip sector and caution ahead of this week's heavy calendar of U.S. economic data dragged share prices to a lower close on Monday.
The Hang Seng Index closed down 35.59 points, or 0.28 percent, at 12,610.17. Turnover was HK$13.91 billion, with the focus mainly on China plays, versus HK$15.15 billion on Friday.

"We saw some profit-taking on the red chips and interest rate uncertainty still prevents people from taking big positions in blue chips," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities.
"The market is a bit cautious ahead of key economic data due this week," he added.
Among other data, the U.S. first quarter employment cost index is due on Tuesday and the April jobs report on Friday.
"People are prepared to sit back and wait to see what happens," said SocGen-Crosby Securities sales trader Miles Remington.

Brokers said late selling in the China plays was prompted by concerns that China may be worried about speculation in the red chip sector. Shares of the Hong Kong-incorporated companies have surged recently on hopes that Chinese parent companies would inject valuable assets into them.

"There are rumours that maybe the people on the China side are not happy to see the red chips stocks so speculative so they might try to slow down asset injections," said Kelvin Tang, an analyst at ImPac Asset Management.
Shares in China Resources Enterprise Ltd fell HK$1.35 to HK$21.85, Ng Fung Hong Ltd shed HK$0.45 to HK$9.90 and China Merchants Hai Hong Holdings Co Ltd lost HK$0.45 to HK$8.10.
"There was a big run on quite a number of red chips. Some people are sitting on big gains on those shares," said Tsang.
But CITIC Pacific Ltd rose HK$0.30 to HK$41.90 on Monday, as investors searched for cheaper red chip issues.
"I think it is seen as a little bit of a laggard. Due to recent movement (in red chips) people are looking for safety. Other counters have spurious earnings," said Remington.
Among other Hang Seng Index components, HSBC Holdings Plc finished the session down HK$0.50 at HK$189.00.
In the property sector, Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd fell HK$0.75 to HK$67.00 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd dropped HK$0.75 to HK$64.00.
The H-share index dropped 22.17 points, or 2.05 percent, to 1,060.03.
April Hang Seng Index futures, which expire on Tuesday, fell 95 points to close at 12,550.
